snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(s_0\) with \(\Gamma(s_0)=\{\tau_0\}\) and \(R\in(0,\infty)\).  Put \(K_R=\bigcup_{(b,h)\in\Lambda_R}\{\eta_b(h)\}\) and let \(\mathcal H_R\) be the compact hyperspace of closed subsets of \(K_R\), including the empty set.  If \(\varphi_h\) is the \(\mathcal N(h,V_0)\) density, then \(v_R<\infty\), the infimum defining \(v_R\) is attained, and it has the explicit semi-infinite linear-program characterization
\[
\begin{aligned}
v_R=\min_{t,Q}\quad &t\\
\text{subject to}\quad
&Q(\,\cdot\mid y)\in\mathcal P(\mathcal H_R)\text{ measurably in }y,\\
&\int_{\mathbb R^d}\!\int_{\mathcal H_R}
  {\bf1}\{\eta_b(h)\in C\}\,Q(dC\mid y)\varphi_h(y)\,dy
  \ge1-\gamma,\quad (b,h)\in\Lambda_R,\\
&\int_{\mathbb R^d}\!\int_{\mathcal H_R}
  \operatorname{diam}(C)\,Q(dC\mid y)\varphi_h(y)\,dy
  \le t,\quad (b,h)\in\Lambda_R.
\end{aligned}
\]
The attaining randomized confidence rules are exactly the measurable uniform-randomizer realizations of the minimizing kernels \(Q\), up to null sets.  This local characterization does not by itself settle finite-sample dominance: changing any proposed pullback at one fixed sample size leaves all its local asymptotic limits unchanged while it can destroy coverage or diameter dominance at that sample size.

defs.def:local-minimax-handle: At a point with \(\Gamma(s_0)=\{\tau_0\}\), analyze the bounded experiment \(\{\mathcal N(h,V_0):(b,h)\in\Lambda_R\}\) with branch target \(\eta_b(h)\), Effros-measurable randomized closed-set rules \(\delta(\mathbb Y_h,U)\), uniform coverage class \(\mathfrak D_R\), and risk \(\mathfrak R_R\); characterize possible minimizers without fixing a candidate rule or proof method.

snapshot.stmt: For every \((a,b)\) in the chain--fork parameter space, the construction in \(\text{def:chain-fork-witness}\) gives two models \(M^{\mathrm{ch}},M^{\mathrm{fk}}\in\mathcal M_3^{\mathrm{df}}\) with the same law pair \((\mathcal N(0,\Sigma^{\mathrm{cf}}(a,b)),\mathcal N(0,\Sigma^{\mathrm{cf}}(a,b)))\), the same empty difference DAG, the same complete equality ledger, and the same empty population LDiffPC output, but \(\tau(M^{\mathrm{ch}})=(a,a,0)\) and \(\tau(M^{\mathrm{fk}})=(0,0,0)\). Therefore every procedure \((D_N)\) having coverage at least \(1-\gamma\) for both models satisfies \(\Pr\{\operatorname{diam}(D_N)\ge\sqrt2|a|\}\ge1-2\gamma\) for every \(N\).

defs.def:chain-fork-witness: For \(p=3\), use the same covariance \(\Sigma^{\mathrm{cf}}(a,b)\) in both environments. One paired SCM has the chain \(X\to Y\to W\), coefficients \(a,b\), and innovations \(1,1-a^2,1-b^2\); the other has the fork \(X\leftarrow Y\to W\), coefficients \(a,b\), and innovations \(1-a^2,1,1-b^2\). In each paired SCM take identical coefficients in both environments, the environment \(1\) model as baseline, and empty target sets. defs.def:conditionally-diff-relevant-path: Given \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\), a path \(\rho\) between \(A\) and \(B\) in \(G_1\cup G_2\) is conditionally diff-relevant relative to \(S\) when it is not diff-relevant and at least one condition holds: \(\rho\) contains a collider having a descendant in \(S\) with an incoming edge in \(D(M)\); \(\rho\) contains a non-collider connected by a path active given \(S\) to a vertex of \(S\setminus\rho\) with an incoming edge in \(D(M)\); or an endpoint of \(\rho\) has an incoming edge along \(\rho\) and a descendant in \(S\) with an incoming edge in \(D(M)\).
defs.def:diff-relevant-path: A path \(\rho\) in \(G_1\cup G_2\) is diff-relevant when either it contains an edge of \(D(M)\), or it contains a non-endpoint vertex having an ancestor with at least one incoming edge in \(D(M)\).
defs.def:diff-separation: For distinct \(A,B\in\mathbb V\) and \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\setminus\{A,B\}\), define \(A\perp_{\mathrm{diff},M}B\mid S\) to hold exactly when \(S\) blocks every diff-relevant path and every conditionally diff-relevant path relative to \(S\) between \(A\) and \(B\) in \(G_1\cup G_2\).
defs.def:difference-dag: For \(M=(G^*,B^*,\mathcal I,G,B,\omega,\pi)\), set \(D(M)=(\mathbb V,E_D(M))\) with \(E_D(M)=\{u\to v:u\in\operatorname{Pa}_{G^*}(v),\ B_{1,uv}\neq B_{2,uv}\}\). The directions are inherited from the baseline DAG.
defs.def:exact-ledger: For \(s=\operatorname{vech}(\boldsymbol\Sigma)\), record for every ordered \(A,B\in\mathbb V\) and every \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\setminus\{A,B\}\) whether \(r_1(A,B\mid S)-r_2(A,B\mid S)=0\), together with every separating set used by the population LDiffPC skeleton and collider rules; the resulting finite record is \(\mathcal L(s)\).

assumptions.ass:diff-faithfulness: For every ordered pair \(A,B\in\mathbb V\) and \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\setminus\{A,B\}\), \(r_1(A,B\mid S)=r_2(A,B\mid S)\) if and only if \(A\perp_{\mathrm{diff},M}B\mid S\), where diff-separation is evaluated on \(G_1\cup G_2\) relative to \(D(M)\).
assumptions.ass:modular-interventions: For every \(e\in\mathbb E\) and \(v\notin\mathcal I_e\), the structural mechanism of \(v\) under \(B_e\) equals its mechanism under \(B^*\).
assumptions.ass:invariant-innovation-variances: The two environments use the same innovation-variance vector \(\omega\).

defs.def:chain-fork-witness:

\]

\[

\]
where the three innovations are mutually independent centered Gaussians with variance vector \(((a^2+1)^{-1},a^2+1,1)\) in coordinate order \((X,Y,W)\). Let \(\mathcal C\) be either \(\mathcal M_3^{\mathrm{df}}\) or \(\mathcal M_3^{\mathrm{BD}}\).  For every \(N\), every confidence procedure satisfying
\[
 \inf_{M\in\mathcal C}\Pr_M\{\tau(M)\in D_N\}\ge1-\gamma
\]
obeys
\[
 \sup_{M\in\mathcal C}\mathbb E_M\!\left[\operatorname{diam}(D_N)\right]=\infty.

Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be closed and semialgebraic, and let \(E\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be compact, full-dimensional, semialgebraic, and regular closed, meaning \(E=\overline{\operatorname{int}E}\). Outside a semialgebraic Lebesgue-null set of translations \(y\),
\[
 C\cap(y+E)=\overline{C\cap(y+\operatorname{int}E)}.
\]
At every such \(y\), put \(D=y+E\). Let \(C_n\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be closed sets converging locally in the Painleve--Kuratowski topology to \(C\), and let \(D_n=y_n+E_n\subseteq\mathbb R^d\). Assume \(\limsup_nD_n\subseteq D\), every compact \(K\subseteq y+\operatorname{int}E\) is contained in \(D_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), and there is a compact \(K_0\) containing \(C_n\cap D_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Then \(\overline{C_n\cap D_n}\to C\cap D\) in the Fell topology, with Hausdorff convergence whenever the limiting intersection is nonempty.

Fix \(s_0\) with \(\Gamma(s_0)=\{\tau_0\}\) and \(R\in(0,\infty)\).  Put \(K_R=\bigcup_{(b,h)\in\Lambda_R}\{\eta_b(h)\}\) and let \(\mathcal H_R\) be the compact hyperspace of closed subsets of \(K_R\), including the empty set.  If \(\varphi_h\) is the \(\mathcal N(h,V_0)\) density, then \(v_R<\infty\), the infimum defining \(v_R\) is attained, and it has the explicit semi-infinite linear-program characterization
\[
\begin{aligned}
v_R=\min_{t,Q}\quad &t\\
\text{subject to}\quad
&Q(\,\cdot\mid y)\in\mathcal P(\mathcal H_R)\text{ measurably in }y,\\
&\int_{\mathbb R^d}\!\int_{\mathcal H_R}
  {\bf1}\{\eta_b(h)\in C\}\,Q(dC\mid y)\varphi_h(y)\,dy
  \ge1-\gamma,\quad (b,h)\in\Lambda_R,\\
&\int_{\mathbb R^d}\!\int_{\mathcal H_R}
  \operatorname{diam}(C)\,Q(dC\mid y)\varphi_h(y)\,dy
  \le t,\quad (b,h)\in\Lambda_R.
\end{aligned}
\]
After the coverage-preserving and diameter-nonincreasing truncation \(C\mapsto C\cap K_R\), the attaining \(\mathcal H_R\)-valued randomized confidence rules are exactly the measurable uniform-randomizer realizations of the minimizing kernels \(Q\), up to null sets.  In particular, every unrestricted attaining rule has an \(\mathcal H_R\)-valued truncation represented by a minimizing kernel, although the unrestricted rule itself need not be supported on \(\mathcal H_R\).  This local characterization does not by itself settle finite-sample dominance: changing any proposed pullback at one fixed sample size leaves all its local asymptotic limits unchanged while it can destroy coverage or diameter dominance at that sample size.

snapshot.stmt:
For every integer \(p\ge3\) and every \((a,b)\) in the chain--fork parameter space, the construction in \(\text{def:chain-fork-witness}\) gives two models \(M^{\mathrm{ch}},M^{\mathrm{fk}}\in\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}\) with the same law pair
\[
 \bigl(\mathcal N(0,\Sigma^{\mathrm{cf}}(a,b)\oplus I_{p-3}),
 \mathcal N(0,\Sigma^{\mathrm{cf}}(a,b)\oplus I_{p-3})\bigr).
\]
Here \(I_0\) denotes the empty covariance block.  The models have the same empty difference DAG, the same complete equality ledger, and the same empty population LDiffPC output, but \(\tau(M^{\mathrm{ch}})=(a,a,0)\) and \(\tau(M^{\mathrm{fk}})=(0,0,0)\).  For every ordered pair of distinct vertices and every eligible conditioning set, each model satisfies diff-faithfulness.  Therefore every procedure \((D_N)\) having coverage at least \(1-\gamma\) for both models satisfies
\[
 \Pr\{\operatorname{diam}(D_N)\ge\sqrt2|a|\}\ge1-2\gamma
\]
for every \(N\).

defs.def:boundary-model-class: \(\mathcal M_p^{\mathrm{df}}=\{M=(G^*,B^*,\mathcal I,G,B,\omega,\pi):\text{ass:linear-structural-equations, ass:baseline-parent-containment, ass:modular-interventions, ass:independent-gaussian-innovations, ass:invariant-innovation-variances, ass:positive-innovation-variances, and ass:diff-faithfulness hold}\}\).
defs.def:chain-fork-witness:
For every integer \(p\ge3\) and every \((a,b)\in\mathbb R^2\) with \(a\neq0\) and \(b\neq0\), choose \(W\in\mathbb V\setminus\{X,Y\}\) and enumerate the remaining vertices as \(\mathbb V\setminus\{X,Y,W\}=\{U_1,\ldots,U_{p-3}\}\).  When \(p=3\), this list is empty and every appended equation and order relation below is vacuous.  Use coordinate order \((X,Y,W,U_1,\ldots,U_{p-3})\).  In each environment of \(M^{\mathrm{ch}}\), define
\[
 X=\varepsilon_X,\qquad Y=aX+\varepsilon_Y,\qquad W=bY+\varepsilon_W,
 \qquad U_j=\varepsilon_{U_j}\quad(1\le j\le p-3),
\]
where all innovations are mutually independent centered Gaussians with variance one.  In each environment of \(M^{\mathrm{fk}}\), define
\[
 Y=\eta_Y,\qquad X=\frac{a}{a^2+1}Y+\eta_X,\qquad W=bY+\eta_W,
 \qquad U_j=\eta_{U_j}\quad(1\le j\le p-3),
\]
where all innovations are mutually independent centered Gaussians, with variance vector
\[
 \bigl((a^2+1)^{-1},a^2+1,1,\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{p-3}\bigr)
\]
in coordinate order \((X,Y,W,U_1,\ldots,U_{p-3})\).  Thus every \(U_j\) is independent of \((X,Y,W)\), has no incident edge, and has the same standard-Gaussian mechanism in both environments.  Within each paired SCM take the two environment coefficient matrices and innovation-variance vectors to be identical, take the displayed DAG and coefficient matrix as \((G^*,B^*)\), and take \(\mathcal I_1=\mathcal I_2=\varnothing\).  Use common orders obtained by appending \(U_1,\ldots,U_{p-3}\) to \(X\prec Y\prec W\) for \(M^{\mathrm{ch}}\) and to \(Y\prec X\prec W\) for \(M^{\mathrm{fk}}\).
defs.def:conditionally-diff-relevant-path: Given \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\), a path \(\rho\) between \(A\) and \(B\) in \(G_1\cup G_2\) is conditionally diff-relevant relative to \(S\) when it is not diff-relevant and at least one condition holds: \(\rho\) contains a collider having a descendant in \(S\) with an incoming edge in \(D(M)\); \(\rho\) contains a non-collider connected by a path active given \(S\) to a vertex of \(S\setminus\rho\) with an incoming edge in \(D(M)\); or an endpoint of \(\rho\) has an incoming edge along \(\rho\) and a descendant in \(S\) with an incoming edge in \(D(M)\).
defs.def:diff-relevant-path: A path \(\rho\) in \(G_1\cup G_2\) is diff-relevant when either it contains an edge of \(D(M)\), or it contains a non-endpoint vertex having an ancestor with at least one incoming edge in \(D(M)\).
defs.def:diff-separation: For distinct \(A,B\in\mathbb V\) and \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\setminus\{A,B\}\), define \(A\perp_{\mathrm{diff},M}B\mid S\) to hold exactly when \(S\) blocks every diff-relevant path and every conditionally diff-relevant path relative to \(S\) between \(A\) and \(B\) in \(G_1\cup G_2\).
defs.def:difference-dag: For \(M=(G^*,B^*,\mathcal I,G,B,\omega,\pi)\), set \(D(M)=(\mathbb V,E_D(M))\) with \(E_D(M)=\{u\to v:u\in\operatorname{Pa}_{G^*}(v),\ B_{1,uv}\neq B_{2,uv}\}\). The directions are inherited from the baseline DAG.
defs.def:exact-ledger: For \(s=\operatorname{vech}(\boldsymbol\Sigma)\), record for every ordered \(A,B\in\mathbb V\) and every \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\setminus\{A,B\}\) whether \(r_1(A,B\mid S)-r_2(A,B\mid S)=0\), together with every separating set used by the population LDiffPC skeleton and collider rules; the resulting finite record is \(\mathcal L(s)\).

assumptions.ass:diff-faithfulness: For every ordered pair \(A,B\in\mathbb V\) and \(S\subseteq\mathbb V\setminus\{A,B\}\), \(r_1(A,B\mid S)=r_2(A,B\mid S)\) if and only if \(A\perp_{\mathrm{diff},M}B\mid S\), where diff-separation is evaluated on \(G_1\cup G_2\) relative to \(D(M)\).
assumptions.ass:independent-gaussian-sampling: Conditional on \(M\), the joint sample law is \(P_{M,1}^{n_1}\otimes P_{M,2}^{n_2}\).
assumptions.ass:invariant-innovation-variances: The two environments use the same innovation-variance vector \(\omega\).
assumptions.ass:modular-interventions: For every \(e\in\mathbb E\) and \(v\notin\mathcal I_e\), the structural mechanism of \(v\) under \(B_e\) equals its mechanism under \(B^*\).
